To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dissolved organic carbon produced by lake phytoplanktons is a mixture of high- and low-molecular-weight compounds, that the high-molecular-weight compounds are not utilized by the bacteria, that the low-molecular-weight components are used by the bacteria, and that the low-molecule-weight components vary in their biochemical composition.

the dissolved organic carbon (DOC) released from natural phytoplankton communities (photosynthetically derived DOC [PDOC]) consists of both low- (MW < 1,000) and high- (MW > 10,000) molecular weight (MW) components, the high-MW PDOC is not utilized by heterotrophic lake bacteria, the low-MW fraction of PDOC is quantitatively more important than the high-MW fraction as a substrate for the bacteria, and
the biochemical composition of the PDOC used by heterotrophs is highly variable and that the high-MW PDOC is not a significant source of bacterial substrates.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the chemical composition and size distribution of the dissolved organic matter (DOM) released from phytoplton and subsequently used by the heterotrophs.
the biochemical composition of dissolved organic carbon released by phytoplankton and used by bacteria.
the role of dissolved organic carbon (DOC) as a substrate for heterotrophic bacteria in lakes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the biochemical composition of the PDOC that was utilized was determined primarily by the composition of the phytoplankter, and the rate of bacterial uptake was determined by the concentration of the substrates and the bacterial community.
the composition of PDO14c is not uniform and that the composition of the PDO14c that is utilized by the hetero-trophic bacteria is not uniform.

the biochemical composition of PDOC is highly variable and is determined by a variety of factors, including the species composition of the phytoplankters and their physiological state, the presence of other dissolved organic compounds, and the presence of humic materials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the low-MW fraction of PDOC was rapidly utilized by bacteria, whereas the high- and intermediate-MW fractions were utilized slowly or were not utilized at all.

the biochemical composition of PDOC and the biochemical composition of the low-Molecular-weight components of PDOC utilized by heterotrophic bacterial are highly dependent upon both the phytoplankter community and environmental conditions.

the heterotrophic bacterioplankton of pelagic environments can utilize PDOC as a substrate for growth, but that the relative importance of PDOC to the bacteria depends upon the nature of the phytoplankters, the nature of the bacterial community, the nature and concentrations of other organic compounds in the environment, and the time of the year.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the composition of dissolved organic matter (DOM) in aquatic systems varies widely, both spatially and temporally, and the composition of DOM is likely to be a key factor in determining the rate of bacterial utilization and the fate of DOM.

the biochemical composition of the low-Molecular-Weight (MW) PDO14C that is utilized by heterotrophic lake bacteria is highly variable and depends on the phytoplankter community and the trophic status of the lake.
the molecular size distribution and chemical composition of dissolved organic carbon (DOC) released from phytoplakton are not always the same.
